sounds.description: Console. A short, soft electronic blip (80 to 120 ms), like a 1960s telemetry readout updating: mid-high pitch, clean, no reverb. 3 or 4 takes, slightly different in pitch, so the repetition doesn't show. Plays every 2 to 4 s (at random), a take at random, softer than everything else, while a camera is live, and stops once telemetry is lost.

Console. An attention tone, not an alarm, short enough to sound three times in 1.5 s (under 0.4 s): a quick rising sweep. Plays when the CAUTION lamp lights: once after a glitch, three times with the lamp's flashes when the controllers save one.

Console. A harsh, urgent alarm pulse in the manner of Apollo's master alarm, cut as a seamless loop of half a second or so, one buzz and its gap. Plays from the reveal of a failure or a catastrophic failure for 3 s, then stops while the lamp stays lit. OGG, for a seamless loop.
Console. Soft radio static with a faint crackle, a seamless loop of 3 to 5 s. Very quiet: it plays under every step without a clip of its own, which is most steps for now. OGG, for a seamless loop.

Console. A dry mechanical click (about 50 to 100 ms): a relay or a toggle switch. Two takes, a press and a release, which the no-repeat deal alternates. Plays on Play and Pause, as the HOLD lamp goes on or off.

Clips. A rocket engine's roar at full thrust, steady in level and pitch, a seamless loop (16 s). Plays while an engine burns on screen: the launch from ignition, the ascent's first and upper stages (the upper one quieter, further off), the retro motors. It carries on from the launch into the ascent without a break. OGG, for a seamless loop.

Clips. An attitude thruster's puff: a short, dry pneumatic hiss (0.5 s). Plays as each jet fires on screen: a capsule turning or braking, a craft backing away, a docking's push, a probe's separation jets and springs, a course correction's puff on the map, the rocket plane's reaction jets; again and again while a jet is stuck open.
Clips. A hatch coming open: a puff and the hiss of the air going (1.6 s). Plays as a spacewalk's or a crew transfer's hatch swings open, and as Voskhod's airlock vents.

Clips. Propellant pumping up the tower: a pump's steady throb, a seamless loop (9.8 s). Plays under the launch preparations while the tanks fill, and stops as they're topped off (or as the pad blows). OGG, for a seamless loop.

Clips. The oxidizer boiling off: a soft, steady hiss, a seamless loop (3.5 s). Plays from the moment the tanks are topped off, on through the countdown, until the engines light at the launch. OGG, for a seamless loop.

Clips. Reentry: a rushing roar of air, a seamless loop (10.3 s). Plays while the heat's glow shows round a capsule, a probe or a carrier coming into an atmosphere, and while the rocket plane's skin glows on its fast run. OGG, for a seamless loop.
Clips. A capsule hitting the sea: a heavy splash (3 s). Plays as the splash shows at splashdown, hard or soft.
Clips. A recovery helicopter hovering some way off: rotor thump and turbine, a seamless loop (35 s). Plays while the helicopter flies in over the recovery. OGG, for a seamless loop.

Clips. A blast and its rumble (5 s). Plays wherever something blows up on screen: a rocket on the pad or in flight, a stage, a craft breaking up in reentry, a carrier burning up, a lander or a probe hitting the ground.

Clips. Two things coming apart: a pyro's crack and a clunk (1.8 s). Plays as springs, bolts, straps or latches fire: a payload pushed off its stage, a stage falling away, modules and packs let go, a lander or a probe released, undocking latches, the ascent stage off the descent stage, the X-15's ventral fin dropped.

Clips. A blast near the ground, its debris coming down (5.3 s). Plays where something blows up on or by the ground: the pad, a rocket falling back onto it, a lander crashing; a blast in the air or in space plays explosion.
Clips. A servomotor's whine (2.3 s). Plays as something mechanical moves: a sampler arm, a dish swinging round, a solar panel turning, a boom drawn in, Lunokhod's lid shut, PrOP-M walking off.
Clips. Something folded unfolding (3.2 s). Plays as booms, whips, wings and masts swing out, ramps come down, a lid or petals open, an adapter's panels open, landing gear comes down.

Music. A short fanfare, about 5 to 10 s, once, when a mission's replay reaches its season summary and the mission didn't fail (glitches, solved or not, don't count). Classic space-age orchestral: bright brass, soaring strings, rising to a confident major-key finish and a clean, decisive ending, no fade. Instrumental. OGG or MP3.

Music. A short sting, about 5 to 10 s, once, when a mission's replay reaches its season summary and the mission failed or ended in catastrophe. Classic space-age orchestral: dark low brass and strings over a held low note, a grinding dissonance that swells to one bitter accent, then a quick collapse into silence. Grave, not horrifying; no triumph. Instrumental. OGG or MP3.
Mission control's room: distant radio chatter and the room's own noise, under the music the whole replay long, never loud enough to follow. A seamless loop of 30 s or more. OGG, for a seamless loop.
